title: From OAuth Profile to Root: Tracing the CVE-2026-94127 Attack Path in F5 BIG-IP APM
summary:
From OAuth Profile to Root: Tracing the CVE-2026-94127 Attack Path in F5 BIG-IP APM


An attacker who wants to exploit CVE-2026-94127 does not need a credential, a session, or a user to click anything. They need a network path to a BIG-IP virtual server that carries an APM access policy and an OAuth profile. F5 rates the flaw 9.8 under CVSS v3.1 and confirms it is being exploited. Walking through the attack path step by step shows why the configuration requirement is easy to satisfy in practice

title: birkly.io is a normal site with a few special needs. Here is what it takes to build it.
summary:
birkly.io is not an overcomplicated website. It has a contact form, a waitlist, donations, sponsor slots, and a club for members. What it does have, like most real projects, is its own special needs. Someone can donate any amount between €1 and €5,000, once or every month, appear on a public supporter list, and join the club with the same email. If they cancel a monthly donation, they keep their account. Only the supporter label on their profile changes.
This post is about why Birkly was built.
